newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Ireland sees little risk if UK stays out of EMU.
newsitem.headline: Ireland sees little risk if UK stays out of EMU.

text.p: Irish Finance Minister Ruairi Quinn said on Monday there would be little risk to Ireland from Britain staying out of monetary union provided sterling maintained a stable relationship with the euro.
"Ireland will qualify for monetary union and we intend to join in the first wave," he said in an interview with Reuters Financial Television.
"If Britain chooses not to join the single currency...there is no real exposure from Ireland's point of view if sterling maintains a stable relationship with the euro," he said.
He said that if, however, sterling were to fall by some 20 percent, for example, studies suggested 28,000 jobs would be lost in Ireland.
But nobody expected this to happen, he said, noting that sterling in fact had been rising in value recently.
"The benefits of joining a single currency outweigh the risks," he added.

He said he believed Britain's destiny lay with the single currency, but if it stayed out of monetary union, in the interim it would be in its interests to maintain a stable relationship between sterling and the euro.
He declined so say whether he thought the Irish punt had risen too sharply recently. "That's a matter for markets to decide for themselves," he said.
